tagline: UNESCO heritage port city of trishaws, street art, and Malaysia's best hawker food.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis exist but often refuse the meter with tourists and quote a flat rate instead; Grab ride-hailing is cheaper, more transparent, and widely used.

emergency.note: 999 is Malaysia's unified emergency number for police, ambulance, and fire; 112 also works as a GSM backup.

hood_desc: The UNESCO World Heritage core of clan jetties, street art, and colonial shophouses centered on Armenian Street and Cannon Square; best for first-time visitors who want temples, mansions, and murals within walking distance.
A vibrant few blocks of sari shops, garland stalls, and banana-leaf restaurants around Lebuh Pasar and Lebuh Queen; suits travelers chasing color, incense, and South Indian food.
George Town's backpacker and nightlife spine, lined with hostels, rooftop bars, and 24-hour hawker food; suits budget travelers and those wanting an easy social scene.
A modern seafront strip of malls, condos, and the famous Gurney Drive hawker centre; good for shopping, seaside strolls, and families wanting comfort chains.
Penang's main beach resort strip on the island's north coast, with a night market and water sports; suits travelers wanting a beach base outside the heritage core.
lodging: Cheong Fatt Tze - The Blue Mansion

transit.hours: Buses generally run about 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; no late-night public transit, so Grab or taxis fill the gap.
transit.pay: Cash fares on board, or tap a Touch 'n Go card / the rapiD Penang app; the free CAT heritage shuttle loops the core at no charge.
transit.note: George Town has no rail or metro as of 2026 (a monorail/LRT is planned but not operating); Rapid Penang buses, the free CAT shuttle, trishaws, and Grab cover the city.

train: No rail on Penang Island; nearest KTM mainline station is in Butterworth across the strait
bus: Intercity/express buses from Sungai Nibong terminal

transit.m: Rapid Penang bus (Route 401E) to city center (~1 hr)

tip.r: Not customary; a 10% service charge is often already added to restaurant bills. Rounding up for good service is appreciated but not expected.

tagline: Caribbean offshore-banking capital ringed by white sand, coral reefs, and cruise ships.

taxi.color: white with a light blue CAYMAN taxi decal
taxi.fareNote: Cayman taxis use government-regulated flat fares by zone rather than meters; confirm the fare for your destination before departing. There is no Uber or Lyft on the islands.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across the Cayman Islands.

hood_desc: The compact capital and cruise port, with the National Museum, duty-free jewelry shops, and government offices around Hog Sty Bay; best for first-timers who want history and walkable dining near the harbor.
Grand Cayman's famous stretch of white sand lined with beachfront resorts, condos, and restaurants; suits travelers who want a classic beach vacation within reach of nightlife.
A planned waterfront town center of boutiques, a cinema, restaurants, and an observation tower between George Town and Seven Mile Beach; good for shopping and family-friendly evenings.
A quieter residential district home to the Cayman Turtle Centre, Hell, and Cemetery Beach; suits travelers wanting local sights and calmer beaches away from the resort strip.
A remote, laid-back stretch of coastline known for its dive sites, blow holes, and the Wreck of the Ten Sail; suits divers and travelers seeking a slower, less touristy pace.
lodging: Hampton by Hilton Grand Cayman Seven Mile Beach
The Westin Grand Cayman Seven Mile Beach Resort & Spa

transit.hours: Privately-run route buses (blue license plates) operate roughly 6am-midnight on main corridors like Seven Mile Beach and George Town; frequency drops sharply off those routes.
transit.pay: Cash fare paid to the driver on boarding (a few CI dollars); no rechargeable transit card.
transit.note: Grand Cayman has no rail or metro. Route buses cover Seven Mile Beach, George Town, and West Bay, but a rental car or taxi is the practical way to reach Camana Bay, East End, or North Side.

bus: Public route buses (Seven Mile Beach, George Town, West Bay corridors)
ferry: Cruise tender service from anchored ships into George Town Harbour (no scheduled inter-island ferries)

transit.m: Taxi to downtown George Town (10 min)
Taxi to Seven Mile Beach (15-20 min)

tip.r: A 10-15% service charge is usually added automatically to restaurant bills; if not, tipping 10-15% is expected. Taxi drivers and hotel staff are typically tipped 10-15%, or a few dollars per bag/service.

tagline: Tohoku castle town famous for a thousand cherry trees, apple orchards, and Meiji-era brick.

taxi.color: varies by company (often black or white)
taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered, clean, and reliable but pricier than buses for a regional city; the GO app helps hail one outside the station area.

emergency.note: 110 reaches police, 119 reaches ambulance/fire; English support is limited outside major cities, and the Japan Visitor Hotline (050-3816-2787) can help translate.

hood_desc: Hirosaki Park surrounds the city's iconic wooden castle keep and is Japan's cherry-blossom epicenter each spring, with moats, gardens, and museums; best for first-time visitors and sakura-season crowds.
A preserved row of Edo-period samurai houses and hedges just north of the castle, offering a quiet step into feudal-era Tsugaru domain life; suits history lovers and photographers.
The area around JR Hirosaki Station and the covered Dobashi shopping street, with everyday shops, apple-themed goods, and easy bus/train access; suits practical travelers who want to be near transit.

A cluster of Meiji- and Taisho-era Western-style buildings, including the former city library and a red-brick church, blending Japanese and European architecture; good for architecture fans and a relaxed stroll.
The rural foothills of Mount Iwaki, ringed by apple orchards and hot-spring inns, with views over the Tsugaru Plain; suits travelers wanting onsen relaxation and countryside scenery.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 7am-9pm; JR trains run until about 10-11pm; there is no late-night service.
transit.pay: Suica/Pasmo-type IC cards work on JR trains; city buses are often cash or local-card only, so check before boarding.
transit.note: Hirosaki's castle and station areas are compact and very walkable; buses and short local rail lines connect outlying sights like Mount Iwaki and the apple orchards.

train: Shin-Aomori Shinkansen station (~40 min away) connects to Tokyo
bus: Highway buses to Aomori, Akita, Sendai, and Tokyo

transit.m: Airport limousine bus to Hirosaki Station (~55 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary and can cause confusion; good service is simply expected and included in the price.

tagline: A volcanic lakeside crossroads on the Rwandan border, living in the shadow of Mount Nyiragongo and an active regional conflict.
rides: None (no established ride-hailing apps; moto-taxis and shared taxi-vans only)

taxi.fareNote: There is no metered taxi fleet; fares for shared 'taxi-bus' minivans and moto-taxi ('moto') rides are agreed before departure, often quoted in a mix of Congolese francs and US dollars.

emergency.police: No functioning nationwide emergency number; contact the nearest PNC (Police Nationale Congolaise) post directly
emergency.medical: No ambulance dispatch line; go directly to a hospital (e.g., HEAL Africa, Charité Maternelle) or arrange transport in advance
emergency.note: DR Congo has no reliable 911/112-style emergency system, and in Goma response capacity is minimal. The city has been intermittently under M23 rebel control since January 2025 as part of the wider eastern DRC conflict, and sits roughly 13-18 km from the active Mount Nyiragongo volcano, which erupted destructively as recently as 2021. Travelers should coordinate safety and evacuation planning through their embassy or an NGO/UN security network rather than relying on local emergency services.

hood_desc: The diplomatic and NGO quarter along the Lake Kivu shorefront, home to the Goma Serena Hotel and most embassies/UN offices; the most secure and orderly part of town for visitors.
A lakeside residential neighborhood with a public beach and several guesthouses, popular with aid workers and longer-term visitors wanting lake access.
A dense, central commercial district around Katindo Market with shops, banks, and budget hotels; the practical hub for everyday errands.
A quieter, greener area near the crater lake Lac Vert (Green Lake) and the foothills toward Mount Mikeno; appeals to those wanting distance from downtown noise.
A crowded, informal market district that is the commercial heart for most residents; authentic but chaotic, with basic budget lodging.

transit.hours: No fixed schedules; informal transport generally runs roughly 6:00 AM to 8-9:00 PM and tapers off after dark for security reasons.
transit.pay: Cash only (Congolese francs or US dollars), paid directly to the driver; moto fares are negotiated per trip.
transit.note: Goma has no formal public transit system, no metro, and no fixed-route buses; getting around relies on shared minibuses, moto-taxis, and private/NGO vehicles, with movement sometimes restricted during periods of insecurity.

air: Goma International Airport (GOM) - service has been severely disrupted since the M23 offensive began in January 2025, with only intermittent commercial flights resuming through 2026
bus: Intercity trucks/buses toward Bukavu and other North Kivu towns, subject to security conditions
ferry: Passenger and cargo boats on Lake Kivu to Bukavu and other lakeshore towns

transit.m: Taxi or moto-taxi to city center

tip.r: Tipping is not customary; rounding up or a small token for good service at hotels and restaurants catering to expats/NGOs is appreciated but optional.

tagline: Rwanda's laid-back Lake Kivu resort town, a short walk from the Congolese border and Goma.

taxi.color: white (car taxis); no fixed color for moto-taxis
taxi.fare: app-based flat/metered pricing where available; negotiated on the street
taxi.fareNote: Yego app-based cabs and motos offer set pricing where coverage exists; street-hailed moto-taxis are more common in Rubavu/Gisenyi and fares should be agreed before the ride.

emergency.note: 112 is Rwanda's general emergency line; the Rwanda National Police also runs dedicated numbers for traffic accidents (113) and fire (111). Rwanda is generally regarded as one of the safer countries in the region, but Rubavu/Gisenyi sits directly across the border from the active eastern DRC conflict, so travelers should keep an eye on the Goma border-crossing situation.

hood_desc: The compact commercial center around the market and main road, with shops, banks, and the town's main restaurants; the practical base for most visitors.
The public lakefront strip with sandy beach, water sports, and beachside bars/hotels; the most tourist-oriented part of town.
A quieter, hillier lakeside area east of downtown known for upscale hotels and lake-view guesthouses.
The bustling neighborhood around the Petite Barrière crossing into Goma, DRC, with cross-border markets and constant foot traffic.
A former colonial mission town a short drive from central Gisenyi, home to a historic cathedral and diocese; quiet and largely residential.
lodging: Kigufi Hill Agape Resort & Kivu Edge

transit.hours: Local transport generally runs from around 5:30 AM to 9-10 PM; intercity coaches to Kigali run through the day with the last departures in early evening.
transit.pay: Cash (Rwandan francs); moto fares negotiated or via the Yego app in town; intercity bus tickets bought at the station or via mobile money.
transit.note: Rubavu/Gisenyi has no formal city bus network; getting around relies on moto-taxis, while intercity coach companies (Volcano Express, RITCO, Virunga Express, and others) run frequent services to Kigali (roughly 3 hours).

air: No scheduled commercial flights; nearest major airport is Kigali International Airport (KGL), about a 3-hour drive
bus: Volcano Express, RITCO, Virunga Express and other coach operators to Kigali and other Rwandan cities
ferry: Informal boat traffic on Lake Kivu; no scheduled passenger ferry service

transit.m: Intercity coach (Volcano Express/RITCO) Kigali to Rubavu

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at hotels/restaurants catering to tourists is appreciated, especially in Rwanda's more formal hospitality sector.

tagline: The bustling capital of Mayotte, a French island department in the Mozambique Channel between Madagascar and the Comoros.
rides: No major international app (Uber/Bolt/Heetch) operates; Taxi Proxi and other licensed radio-taxi dispatch services only

taxi.fare: metered in town; fixed zone fares for taxi brousse (shared taxis)
taxi.fareNote: Licensed taxis are metered; shared 'taxi brousse' minivans charge fixed zone-based fares (roughly €1.40 in town by day, €2.10 at night, up to about €6.20 for the longest cross-island routes).

emergency.note: As an overseas French department, Mayotte uses standard French emergency numbers (15 medical/SAMU, 17 police/gendarmerie, 18 fire/pompiers, 112 general EU number) with a functioning hospital system (Centre Hospitalier de Mayotte). That said, Mayotte has faced significant social unrest, water shortages, and elevated crime/gang-related violence in recent years compared to mainland France, particularly around informal settlements; travelers should check current conditions before visiting.

hood_desc: The commercial and administrative heart of the island around the Hôtel de Ville and Place du Marché, with banks, ferry access, and most restaurants; the natural base for visitors.
Mayotte's oldest and largest district at the town's north end, now a dense industrial and residential zone with major markets; authentic but not geared toward tourism.
A central residential neighborhood home to the island's main hospital and several administrative offices; convenient and workaday rather than scenic.
A coastal area a couple of kilometers south of downtown with a resort-style lodge and beach access; the closest thing to a resort enclave near Mamoudzou.
A hillside residential district housing the main stadium (Stade Cavani); quieter, mostly local, with sweeping views over the lagoon.

transit.hours: Taxis brousse run roughly 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM, with reduced, higher-fare service until around 11:00 PM; there is no late-night network.
transit.pay: Cash (euros); fixed zone-based fares are paid directly to the driver.
transit.note: Mayotte has no metro or rail system; shared taxis brousse are the main public transport on Grande-Terre, supplemented by 'la barge,' the car/passenger ferry linking Mamoudzou to Dzaoudzi/Petite-Terre and the airport.

air: Dzaoudzi-Pamandzi International Airport (DZA), on Petite-Terre, reached from Mamoudzou via the La Barge car ferry (about a 15-minute crossing)
bus: Taxi brousse (shared bush taxis) across Grande-Terre
ferry: La Barge car/passenger ferry between Mamoudzou and Dzaoudzi/Petite-Terre
Tourist boat trips to Petite-Terre and the lagoon islets

airport.name: Dzaoudzi-Pamandzi International Airport (DZA)
airport.drive: ~15-min ferry crossing plus a short drive

transit.m: La Barge car/passenger ferry to Mamoudzou (about 15 min, frequent)
Taxi from the ferry landing to the city center

tip.r: As in mainland France, tipping is not expected since service is generally included in restaurant prices; rounding up is welcome but optional.

tagline: Highland capital of Tigray, gateway to Aksumite history and the otherworldly Danakil Depression.

taxi.fareNote: Shared minibus 'line taxis' run fixed routes for a small flat fare; private trips in blue-and-white taxis are not metered, so agree the fare before departure.

emergency.note: 911 is a general emergency line but is not always reliably staffed; hotel or tour operator assistance is often faster in practice.

hood_desc: The commercial and administrative heart of Mekelle around the central square and Yohannes IV Palace Museum; best base for first-time visitors who want everything walkable.
A busy hotel and business district near the Tigray Martyrs' Memorial Monument, popular with conference travelers and NGO staff, with the city's liveliest restaurants and bars.
A largely residential district built around the well-known Ayder Referral Hospital; quiet and mostly local, with few tourist services.
A university district home to Mekelle University's Adi-Haki campus, with budget guesthouses and student-oriented cafes.
An outlying district near Alula Aba Nega International Airport, semi-rural and convenient for early flights but far from the center.

transit.hours: Shared minibuses and Bajaj tuk-tuks run roughly 6:00 AM to 8:00-9:00 PM; little to no public transport after dark.
transit.pay: Cash paid directly to the driver or conductor; there is no rechargeable transit card system.
transit.note: There is no metro, tram, or formal city bus network; shared minibuses and blue three-wheeled Bajaj tuk-tuks are the main way to get around.

bus: Selam Bus and Sky Bus intercity coaches to Addis Ababa

tip.r: Not obligatory, but rounding up or leaving 5-10% at hotels and restaurants catering to travelers is appreciated.

tagline: Medieval canal city of cobblestones, chocolate shops, and Flemish Primitive art.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are metered with fixed start-up and per-km rates set by the city; ranks are at the Markt, the train station, and major hotels.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number and connects to police, fire, and ambulance.

hood_desc: The postcard core of Bruges around the Markt, Belfry, and Burg square, packed with museums, chocolate shops, and canal-boat docks; best for first-timers who want everything within walking distance, though it's also the most crowded with day-trippers.
A quieter, more residential quarter east of the centre around the Jerusalem Church and the Lace Centre; good for travelers wanting an authentic feel a short walk from the sights.
A laid-back local neighborhood northwest of the centre with independent cafes and the Sint-Gilliskerk; suited to travelers wanting a residential, non-touristy base.
The area around Bruges railway station, with easy access to trains and buses; practical for budget travelers and those arriving late or leaving early.
A green, largely residential suburb south of the centre near Beisbroek Park and the Tillegembos woods; suited to families and nature-minded travelers wanting space and quiet.

transit.hours: Buses generally run from about 6:00 AM to midnight; Bruges has no metro or tram.
transit.pay: Contactless bank card or the De Lijn app are standard; single tickets can also be bought from the driver at a surcharge.
transit.note: Bruges has no metro or tram; De Lijn buses radiate from the train station and Markt, but the compact historic centre is easily explored on foot or by bike.

train: Brugge railway station (NMBS/SNCB intercity trains to Brussels, Ghent, Ostend)
ferry: P&O Ferries/DFDS via nearby Zeebrugge (UK connections)

transit.m: Direct train Brussels Airport to Bruges (~70 min, hourly)

tip.r: Service is usually included in the bill; rounding up or leaving small change (5-10%) for good service is appreciated but not expected.

tagline: Riverside Miao and Tujia old town of stilt houses, covered bridges, and lantern-lit nights on the Tuo River.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis exist but are limited since the pedestrianized old town is car-free; most visitors use the Didi ride-hailing app or walk.

emergency.note: 119 is for fire; English-speaking operators are not guaranteed, so hotel staff assistance is recommended.

hood_desc: The scenic heart of Fenghuang along the Tuo River, lined with stilted wooden houses (diaojiaolou), riverside bars, and boat docks; the liveliest and most photographed area, especially at night.
A quieter residential quarter around the historic East Gate Tower and old city wall; good for travelers wanting easy access to the sights without the nightlife crowds.
A calmer district near the North Gate Tower with local shops and fewer tourists than the riverside; suited to travelers wanting an everyday, authentic feel.
The area around the iconic covered Hong Bridge (Rainbow Bridge) lined with shops; central and highly touristy, close to most major sights.
The old market street near the Former Residence of Shen Congwen, lined with souvenir stalls, teahouses, and snack vendors; good for shopping and street food.
lodging: Fenghuang Old Town International Youth Hostel
Fenghuang Old Town International Youth Hostel
Fenghuang Old Town International Youth Hostel

transit.hours: Local buses run roughly 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM; the old town itself is pedestrianized and explored on foot.
transit.pay: Cash or mobile payment (Alipay/WeChat Pay) on board; no rechargeable transit card for casual visitors.
transit.note: The ancient town core is pedestrianized and car-free; buses and taxis are used mainly to reach the long-distance bus station or nearby attractions like Qiliang Cave.

train: Jishou East railway station (high-speed rail, ~1 hr away)
bus: Fenghuang long-distance bus station (coaches to Jishou, Zhangjiajie, Changsha)

car.idp: Not valid; Chinese driving license required

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to Fenghuang (~45 min, several times daily)

tip.r: Tipping is not expected or customary in China, including in Fenghuang; a small tip for a very helpful private guide is fine but never required.
